requirements.requirement: Persistent host firewall on node1 allows SSH from any address
requirements.summary: firewalld public zone permanently includes the ssh service with no source restriction (cmd-111ff621759b4393). Live connectivity confirmed from both node2 and node3 (TCP reaches sshd auth stage, not blocked) both before and after node1's restart (cmd-d886e20712a54749, cmd-a1dae38a50134251).

requirements.requirement: TCP port 9000 allowed only from node2
requirements.summary: A permanent rich rule with explicit priority -100 accepts tcp/9000 from node2's IP in the pre-chain, evaluated before the generic reject in the post-chain (cmd-e66ead8d8cec4945, cmd-6c74584691a74bff, cmd-2e7acd58aa144d93). Live curl from node2 to node1:9000 returned HTTP 200 both before and after node1's and node2's restarts (cmd-d886e20712a54749, cmd-0107036bf2034d78, cmd-8d1cd4ce33b74208).

requirements.requirement: TCP port 9000 rejected from node3 and everywhere else
requirements.summary: A permanent, unscoped rich reject rule (priority 100) covers all sources not explicitly accepted. Live curl from node3 to node1:9000 returned 'Connection refused' both before and after node1's and node3's restarts (cmd-e9cf686f305e49f2, cmd-3ed83fae42ca413a, cmd-a1dae38a50134251).

requirements.requirement: Firewall configuration is persistent (enabled, survives reboot)
requirements.summary: Rules were added with --permanent and firewalld is enabled+active (cmd-7658aaa61e4b40c4). firewall-cmd --list-all shows identical rich rules with the same priorities both before node1's reboot (cmd-05ba649be3a44021) and after it (cmd-c3dad666c4134fa2), and behavior was re-verified live post-reboot.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart protocol: node1 pre/post boot identity, restart, recovered firewall/service state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id d6298ced captured while firewalld was active (cmd-102ad427018b4786), reboot acknowledged (cmd-17ec4a0bc66b4897), node unreachable during the transition (cmd-d3f62bf635e44afe), new boot_id 535ebb5b with uptime 2.81s confirms restart (cmd-3159fd352fba4fde), firewalld and rules confirmed intact (cmd-c3dad666c4134fa2) and live accept/reject behavior re-verified (cmd-0107036bf2034d78, cmd-3ed83fae42ca413a). Cross-checked against fixed before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity snapshots showing the same d6298ced→535ebb5b transition.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart protocol: node2 pre/post boot identity, restart, recovered state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 5fb1b173 captured (cmd-1b8f3508176d41a1), reboot acknowledged (cmd-e8be0776d2e84b81), node unreachable during transition (cmd-3505d8b6fc864e2e, cmd-215329a4f4e7430c), new boot_id f0e58231 with uptime 3.55s confirms restart (cmd-f9cb5bfb074c47a1), and node2's ability to reach node1:9000 was re-verified post-restart confirming its networking and the firewall policy both recovered correctly (cmd-8d1cd4ce33b74208). Cross-checked against fixed lifecycle snapshots showing the same boot-id transition.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart protocol: node3 pre/post boot identity, restart, recovered state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id c2ffc729 captured (cmd-1243be5506bb4df7), reboot acknowledged (cmd-b5b63002bb2a4982), node unreachable during transition (cmd-fb3c5e6f8e8e4a5d, cmd-3d9bc3004ece452e), new boot_id 45476c58 with uptime 3.38s confirms restart (cmd-1e3ba1580f7e4730), and post-restart the reject behavior and SSH reachability were re-verified confirming node3's networking recovered and the firewall policy remains correctly enforced (cmd-a1dae38a50134251). Cross-checked against fixed lifecycle snapshots showing the same boot-id transition.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are directly satisfied with live evidence: node1's firewalld permanently allows SSH from any source, permanently allows TCP/9000 only from node2 via a correctly prioritized rich rule, and permanently rejects TCP/9000 from node3/everywhere else via a generic reject rule. The configuration was verified to persist and remain correctly enforced across a full reboot of node1 itself, and the required provider-wide restart protocol was also completed and evidenced for node2 and node3, each showing pre-restart baseline, unreachability during reboot, a changed boot identity, and recovered, correctly-functioning state. Hygiene is high; the only blemish is a small leftover /tmp/reboot.log file on node2 and node3.
limitations: Only three nodes exist in this topology (node1, node2, node3), so 'everywhere else' for the reject rule is verified only against node3 and the generic (source-unrestricted) reject rule structure, not against an exhaustive set of other IPs.

The connectivity tests used a temporary python http.server rather than a persistent production service on port 9000, but this is an equivalent, low-risk method of exercising the firewall path and does not affect confidence in the firewall verdict.

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing actions were mostly bounded and purposeful: an initial rich-rule pair (cmd-b6ca2bc62d6b497c) had a chain-ordering bug and was replaced with correctly prioritized rules (cmd-e66ead8d8cec4945), which is a valid corrective action rather than an unnecessary mutation. Temporary HTTP listeners on node1 (cmd-85dfee313b2c4396, cmd-2dcfdbd2a5dc4d14, cmd-ec20fdc9bad348dd, cmd-ae57d302e6124c6c) were used solely to produce bounded connectivity evidence and were each killed shortly after (cmd-7658aaa61e4b40c4, cmd-8b74e9fa67434578, cmd-e6e89b218f804a82, cmd-d85cfdf244624b5b), with pid/log files removed in the final cleanup on node1. The three systemctl reboots (cmd-17ec4a0bc66b4897, cmd-e8be0776d2e84b81, cmd-b5b63002bb2a4982) are required by the mandated restart-evidence protocol, not task-driven mutations. One minor residue: the nohup wrapper scripts used to trigger reboots on node2 and node3 wrote /tmp/reboot.log on those nodes, and unlike node1 (where it was removed by cmd-d85cfdf244624b5b), these files were left behind, visible as additions in the after_executor temporary-files diff for node2 and node3. This is low-risk, non-sensitive leftover residue rather than a security or functional issue.
